content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I want an angular plate with two quadratic plates positioned in right angel to each other. The edge length of the plates is 140mm. They are 10mm thick. On one of the two plates I would like to have a quadratic cutout, 45x45mm, centred on the plate. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept – step by step (no execution yet)

1. Establish the first square plate lying flat in the XY-plane  
   • Use a block element with the full 140 mm edge lengths in X and Y and the 10 mm thickness in Z.  
   • Basepoint at (0 , 0 , 0) so it occupies X = 0-140, Y = 0-140, Z = 0-10.  
   • subtraction = False (this is the initial, positive volume).

2. Add the second square plate, standing upright and perpendicular to the first one  
   • Block 10 mm thick in X, 140 mm high in Z, 140 mm long in Y.  
   • Basepoint again at (0 , 0 , 0); this makes it span X = 0-10, Y = 0-140, Z = 0-140.  
   • The two plates now share the 10×140×10 corner volume, forming a rigid 90° “L”.

3. Create the centred quadratic cut-out in the flat plate  
   • A third block with size 45 × 45 × 10 mm (thickness matches the plate),  
     centred on the plate → its lower-left-bottom corner is  
     (70-22.5, 70-22.5, 0) = (47.5 , 47.5 , 0).  
   • subtraction = True so this volume is removed.

4. Combine everything in one single functions.block(…) call by supplying three entries in every array argument:  
   x_size  = [140,  10,  45]  
   y_size  = [140, 140,  45]  
   z_size  = [ 10, 140,  10]  
   x       = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   y       = [  0,   0, 47.5]  
   z       = [  0,   0,    0]  
   subtraction = [False, False, True]

5. Once approved, this block(…) call can be followed by functions.finished(allFunctionsCalled=True) to close the modelling sequence.

Let me know and I will prepare the exact function call for execution.
